title: Can Cognitive Flexibility Serve as a Critical Bridge Between Impulsivity and Loneliness?
abstract: In this study, it was aimed to test the theoretical model developed about the mediating role of cognitive flexibility in the relationship between impulsivity and loneliness. This study, which was designed based on the correlational model, included a sample group of 459 secondary school students, 228 girls (49.7%) and 231 boys (50.3%). Demographic Information Form, Barrat Impulsivity Scale-11, Cognitive Flexibility Scale and Children’s Loneliness Scale were used as data collection tools. According to the correlation analysis, it was determined that there was a positive relationship between impulsivity and loneliness, and a negative relationship between cognitive flexibility with impulsivity and loneliness. According to the results of the Structural Equation Model analysis, cognitive flexibility mediates the relationship between impulsivity and loneliness. This study can be a resource for school mental health professionals in the planning of protective and preventive intervention studies.
